what_it_does: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) is a technique where an AI language model, instead of relying only on what it learned during training, also searches a large external knowledge base at query time and uses the retrieved passages to give a better answer. This creates two distinct bottlenecks: the search step jumps around the knowledge base in an irregular pattern that underuses memory bandwidth, while the answer-generation step is limited by how fast model weights can be streamed from memory. The paper proposes HeterRAG, which uses two different kinds of memory-with-built-in-computation (called processing-in-memory, or PIM — chips where small computing circuits sit inside the memory itself to avoid slow trips over the data bus): cheaper, higher-capacity DIMM-based PIM modules (similar to ordinary RAM sticks but with compute) handle the irregular search lookups; faster, narrower HBM-based PIM (a stacked high-bandwidth memory chip common in AI accelerators) handles the high-throughput generation phase. Matching each task to the right memory type is the core contribution. This is based solely on the abstract.
